questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the correct form of the verb: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Subject 'She' is third person singular, so the verb takes 's' in simple present tense: 'goes'.
questions.concept: Subject-verb agreement in simple present tense.
questions.tip: Third person singular subjects (he/she/it) need 's' or 'es' added to the base verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Its a beautiful day isnt it
It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
Its' a beautiful day isn't it
It is a beautiful day isnt it?
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is' and needs an apostrophe; the sentence needs a comma before the tag question and a question mark at the end.
questions.concept: Apostrophe use in contractions and tag-question punctuation.
questions.tip: Never confuse 'its' (possessive) with 'it's' (it is).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ happy with the result.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it — here 'students' (plural), so 'were' is correct.
questions.tip: In neither/nor and either/or constructions, match the verb to the nearer subject.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the sentence with correct use of the subjunctive mood.
options: If I was you, I would apologise.
If I were you, I would apologise.
If I am you, I would apologise.
If I will be you, I would apologise.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood for hypothetical/unreal conditions uses 'were' regardless of subject: 'If I were you...'.
questions.tip: Use 'were' (not 'was') after 'if' for imaginary or contrary-to-fact situations.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the correct synonym of 'Benevolent'.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly; 'Kind' is the closest synonym among the options.
questions.tip: Break the word into roots: 'bene-' means good/well, as in benefit, benefactor.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the correct antonym of 'Frugal'.
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means careful with money/resources; its opposite is 'Extravagant' (spending excessively).
questions.tip: If three options are near-synonyms and one is very different, the odd one out is usually the antonym.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'Ubiquitous'.
questions.explanation: 'Ubiquitous' means present everywhere; 'Omnipresent' carries the same meaning.
questions.tip: Learn vocabulary in word families: ubiquity, ubiquitous, ubiquitously.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Passage: 'Water scarcity is one of the greatest challenges of the twenty-first century. As populations grow and climate patterns shift, many regions face reduced access to clean drinking water.' What is the passage mainly about?
options: Water scarcity is a major modern challenge
questions.explanation: The passage's main idea, stated in the first sentence, is that water scarcity is a major challenge of this century.
questions.concept: Identifying the main idea of a short passage.
questions.tip: The main idea is often stated directly in the first or last sentence of a short passage.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Passage: 'Although renewable energy sources are becoming cheaper, their adoption still lags in many developing countries due to high upfront infrastructure costs, despite long-term savings.' What does the passage imply?
options: Renewable energy is never adopted in developing countries
Upfront cost is a barrier even when long-term savings exist
Developing countries do not want renewable energy
questions.explanation: The passage states adoption 'lags... due to high upfront infrastructure costs, despite long-term savings', implying cost is the barrier even though it pays off later.
questions.concept: Drawing inference from a complex sentence with a contrast clause ('despite').
questions.tip: Pay close attention to contrast words like 'although', 'despite', and 'however' — they often hold the real meaning.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Spot the error: 'Each of the students have submitted their assignment.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be 'has submitted', not 'have submitted'.
questions.tip: 'Each', 'every', 'either', and 'neither' always take a singular verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Spot the error: 'She don't like to travel alone at night.'
questions.explanation: With the third person singular subject 'She', the correct auxiliary is 'doesn't', not 'don't'.
questions.concept: Auxiliary verb agreement in negative sentences.
questions.tip: Use 'doesn't' with he/she/it, and 'don't' with I/you/we/they.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Spot the error: 'The number of accidents on this road have increased this year.'
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has increased'); it is 'a number of' (meaning several) that takes a plural verb.
questions.concept: Distinguishing 'the number of' (singular) from 'a number of' (plural).
questions.tip: 'The number of X' = singular verb. 'A number of X' = plural verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Improve the underlined part: 'He is working in this company since 2015.'
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing to the present with 'since' requires the present perfect continuous tense: 'has been working'.
questions.tip: Use 'has/have been + verb-ing' with 'since' (a point in time) or 'for' (a duration).

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Improve the sentence: 'Despite of the rain, the match continued.'
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'; the correct form is simply 'Despite the rain'.
questions.concept: Correct usage of 'despite' vs 'in spite of'.
questions.tip: 'Despite' = no 'of' needed. 'In spite of' = 'of' needed. Never mix them.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank: Technology has made communication ___ easier than it was two decades ago.
questions.explanation: 'Much' is used before comparative adjectives like 'easier' to intensify them; 'many' is used with countable nouns, not comparatives.
questions.tip: Use 'much/far/a lot' before comparatives (easier, bigger), not 'many' or 'more much'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Fill in the blank: She was so tired that she ___ asleep as soon as she sat down.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the simple past tense ('was tired'), so the next verb should also be in simple past: 'fell'.
questions.tip: Keep tenses consistent across a sentence unless there is a clear reason to shift (like reported speech).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Doctor is to Hospital as Teacher is to ?
questions.explanation: A Doctor works in a Hospital; similarly, a Teacher works in a School. The relationship is 'person : workplace'.
questions.tip: First state the relationship between the given pair in words, then apply the same relationship to find the answer.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Pen is to Write as Scissors is to ?
questions.explanation: A Pen is used to Write; similarly, Scissors are used to Cut. The relationship is 'tool : function'.
questions.tip: Focus on the primary action the tool performs, not related nouns like 'blade' or 'paper'.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Find the next number in the series: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the previous term (2×2=4, 4×2=8, 8×2=16, 16×2=32).
questions.concept: Geometric progression (multiply by a constant ratio).
questions.tip: Check the ratio between consecutive terms first; if constant, it's a geometric series.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Find the missing term: 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows the pattern (previous term × 2) + 1: 3×2+1=7, 7×2+1=15, 15×2+1=31, 31×2+1=63.
questions.concept: Series with a combined multiply-and-add pattern.
questions.tip: When simple addition/multiplication doesn't fit, try a combined rule like ×2+1.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded in the same pattern?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1 in the alphabet: C→D, A→B, T→U. Applying this to DOG: D→E, O→P, G→H, giving EPH.
questions.concept: Letter-shift coding pattern (+1 to each letter).
questions.tip: Compare each letter's position change between the code word and original word to find the shift rule.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: In a certain code, 'ROSE' is written as '6821' and 'CHAIR' is written as '73456'. How is 'SEARCH' coded?
questions.explanation: From ROSE=6821: R=6,O=8,S=2,E=1. From CHAIR=73456: C=7,H=3,A=4,I=5,R=6 (consistent with R=6 from ROSE). So S=2,E=1,A=4,R=6,C=7,H=3. SEARCH = S,E,A,R,C,H → 2,1,4,6,7,3 → 214673.
questions.tip: Build a letter-to-digit map from all given clues before decoding the new word, and double check for repeated letters/digits.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Pointing to a photograph, Rahul said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl in the photo related to Rahul?
questions.explanation: Grandfather's only son is Rahul's father (since Rahul is male and descended from this line). The daughter of Rahul's father is Rahul's sister.
questions.tip: Convert each clue into a direct relation step by step, starting from the fixed reference person.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: A is B's brother. C is D's mother and A's wife. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: C is A's wife and D's mother, meaning A and C are D's parents. So D is A's son or daughter.
questions.concept: Direct family relation from parent-spouse clues.
questions.tip: If someone is described as the spouse of a person and the parent of another, that other person is their child.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Raj walks 5 km North, then turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: After walking North 5 km, turning right (East) 3 km, then turning right again (South) 5 km, Raj ends up 3 km East of the starting point — the two 5 km legs cancel out vertically.
questions.concept: Net displacement in direction problems using a mental grid.
questions.tip: Plot each move on an imaginary x-y grid (North=+y, East=+x) and compute net horizontal/vertical displacement separately.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: If you are facing East and turn 90° clockwise, which direction are you now facing?
questions.explanation: Turning 90° clockwise from East takes you to South (East → South → West → North in clockwise order).
questions.tip: Memorise the clockwise order: North → East → South → West → North.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Statements: All pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers. Conclusion I: All pens are erasers. Conclusion II: Some erasers are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Since all pens are pencils and all pencils are erasers, all pens are erasers (I follows). Also, since all pens are erasers, at least some erasers are pens (II follows).
questions.concept: Chain syllogism with universal affirmative statements.
questions.tip: Draw a simple Venn diagram: when A⊆B and B⊆C, then A⊆C, and reversing a universal statement gives a valid 'some' conclusion.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. B sits immediately to the right of A. C sits at one of the ends. D sits immediately left of E. If A sits second from the left, which of these could be the correct order from left to right?
questions.explanation: C at one end, A second from left, B immediately right of A, and D immediately left of E all fit: C, A, B, D, E satisfies every condition.
questions.concept: Linear seating arrangement with multiple constraints.
questions.tip: Fix the most restrictive clue first (here, A's fixed position), then place relative clues (immediately left/right) around it.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Six people sit around a circular table facing the centre. P is exactly third to the right of Q. Where does P sit relative to Q?
questions.explanation: With 6 people seated in a circle, being 3 seats away (exactly half of 6) from someone means sitting directly opposite them, i.e., diagonally opposite.
questions.tip: In a circle of N people, being 'N/2 seats' away from someone means sitting directly opposite them.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.text: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship between 'Fruits', 'Mangoes', and 'Vehicles'?
options: Three separate non-overlapping circles with Mangoes fully inside Fruits
Three overlapping circles, all intersecting each other
One circle inside another, both overlapping Vehicles
questions.explanation: Mangoes are a type of Fruit (so Mangoes should be a smaller circle fully inside Fruits), while Vehicles are unrelated to both and should be a separate, non-overlapping circle.
questions.concept: Representing category relationships (subset vs unrelated) with Venn diagrams.
questions.tip: Ask: is one group fully part of another (subset), partly overlapping, or completely unrelated — then choose the diagram matching that logic.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: What is the sum of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.explanation: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2 = 10×11/2 = 55.
questions.concept: Sum of first n natural numbers formula.
questions.tip: Memorise n(n+1)/2 for sum of natural numbers — it appears frequently in SSC exams.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: Find the largest number that exactly divides 70 and 105.
questions.explanation: HCF of 70 and 105: 70=2×5×7, 105=3×5×7, common factors are 5×7=35.
questions.concept: Highest Common Factor (HCF) by prime factorization.
questions.tip: Prime-factorize both numbers, then multiply the common prime factors to get the HCF.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: What is 25% of 240?
questions.tip: 25% equals 1/4, so dividing the number by 4 gives the same answer quickly.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: The price of an item is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in price?
questions.explanation: Net change = -(a×b)/100 where a=b=20, so -20×20/100 = -4%, i.e., a 4% decrease overall.
questions.tip: When a quantity increases by x% then decreases by x%, the net effect is always a decrease of x²/100 percent.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: Divide ₹1200 between A and B in the ratio 3:5. What is B's share?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 3+5 = 8. B's share = (5/8) × 1200 = ₹750.
questions.concept: Dividing a quantity in a given ratio.
questions.tip: Divide the total by the sum of ratio parts first, then multiply by each person's number of parts.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹400 and sells it for ₹460. What is his profit percentage?
questions.tip: Profit% is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP), not the Selling Price (SP).

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: A can complete a work in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. Working together, how many days will they take?
questions.concept: Combined work rate using LCM method.
questions.tip: Add individual work rates (1/days) to get the combined rate, then take the reciprocal for total time.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: A train travels 300 km in 5 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance/Time = 300/5 = 60 km/h.
questions.tip: Speed = Distance ÷ Time — always keep units consistent (km and hours, or m and seconds).

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: Find the simple interest on ₹5000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
questions.tip: Memorise SI = PRT/100 where P=Principal, R=Rate per annum, T=Time in years.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: Find the average of 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50.
questions.tip: Average = Sum of all values ÷ Number of values.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.tip: Memorise this identity — it is a very common SSC algebra shortcut.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Sum of angles = 180°. Total ratio parts = 2+3+4=9. Largest angle = (4/9)×180 = 80°.
questions.concept: Triangle angle sum property with ratio division.
questions.tip: The three angles of any triangle always sum to 180°; use this with the given ratio to find each angle.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: What is the value of sin(30°) + cos(60°)?
questions.explanation: sin(30°) = 0.5 and cos(60°) = 0.5, so their sum is 0.5+0.5 = 1.
questions.concept: Standard trigonometric values at common angles.
questions.tip: Memorise sin/cos/tan values for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° — they are asked frequently in SSC exams.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: Find the area of a rectangle with length 12 cm and breadth 7 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle = length × breadth = 12 × 7 = 84 cm².
questions.tip: Area = length × breadth; perimeter = 2×(length+breadth). Don't confuse the two.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.text: A pie chart shows that a company spends 25% of its budget on salaries. If the total budget is ₹8,00,000, how much is spent on salaries?
questions.concept: Reading percentage values from a pie chart.
questions.tip: In pie-chart questions, convert the given percentage directly against the stated total to find the actual value.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: Who is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi is officially recognised as the 'Father of the Nation' in India.
questions.tip: This is a commonly repeated static GK fact in SSC exams — know key national titles.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is the longest river flowing within India, stretching about 2,525 km.
questions.tip: Know the top 3-4 longest Indian rivers; this topic repeats often in SSC General Awareness.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is primarily responsible for regulating which of the following?
options: The banking and monetary system of India
questions.explanation: The RBI is India's central bank, responsible for regulating the banking system and monetary policy (interest rates, money supply).
questions.concept: Role of the Reserve Bank of India.
questions.tip: RBI = monetary policy and banking regulation; SEBI = stock markets; Finance Ministry = taxes and budget.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO2) from the air and release oxygen during photosynthesis.
questions.tip: Remember: plants take in CO2 and water, and release O2 and glucose during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: The SI unit of electric current is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), named after André-Marie Ampère.
questions.concept: SI units of common physical quantities.
questions.tip: Learn SI units for current (Ampere), voltage (Volt), resistance (Ohm), and power (Watt) together — they're often confused.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award. In which field can it be awarded?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna can be awarded for exceptional service/performance in any field of human endeavour, not restricted to one domain.
questions.tip: Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award; the Padma awards (Shri/Bhushan/Vibhushan) are the next tier.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: Who wrote the book 'Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: 'The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort in 1944.
questions.concept: Famous Indian books and their authors.
questions.tip: Static GK often pairs freedom fighters with their famous books — make a quick revision list.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.text: World Environment Day is observed on which date?
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is observed annually on 5 June to raise awareness about environmental protection.
questions.tip: 22 April is Earth Day, 1 May is Labour Day, and 14 November is Children's Day in India — don't mix these up.
